closing as stale. if you want to continue, pls ping and can re-open.

Its a shame that such a trivial fix to a modestly common bug stalled out like this, one that just bit me hard today. @EvsanDlg if you don't object, I'd be willing to add a test, cherrypick `4fb57b2` as a starting point (so you get commit credit), and add types to everything plus any other housekeeping (changelog entry, etc), presumably in a new PR. 

A few pandas-specific questions on the finer details of your conventions and style:

@ivanovmg @jreback Is there a reason `test_table` uses the `_check_plot_works` helper for `DataFrame.plot(table=True)` but not `pandas.plotting.table` (as @EvsanDlg demonstrates in their example)? Also, just to confirm since I couldn't find it in the docs, is `unittest.mock.patch` the canonical pandas way of mocking/patching (vs. e.g. monkeypath, pytest-mocker, etc), and from `from unittest.mock import patch` the standard pandas convention for importing it (vs import `unittest.mock` and referring to it explicitly)?

Also, @jreback should this get a versionchanged marker, so users understand these arguments are non-functional in prior versions of pandas? If so, any particular guidance on phrasing? Thanks!

@CAM-Gerlach, ``_check_plot_works`` does more than simply run a plotting function: it ensures that the figure is closed afterwards, that it is saveable and that the returned object is of the correct type.

Since my previous comment here on the use of ``unittest.mock.patch`` I attempted to submit a PR, where I used mocking. It got rejected by the CI. If I remember correctly, it seemed that the CI did not like the use of ``patch`` (I'm not sure whether it was because of importing it in particular way, or just ``patch`` was banned, period).

Throughout the code base I saw the use of ``monkeypatch`` in multiple places, though.
Thus, my comment on ``unittest.mock.patch`` should be reconsidered.
I am not sure if using ``monkeypatch`` one can check whether ``matplotlib.pyplot.table`` was called correctly.

issue_context.title: BUG: rowLabels and colLabels args in pandas.plotting.table have no effect
issue_context.body:
- [ yes ] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.

- [ yes ] I have confirmed this bug exists on the latest version of pandas.

- [ yes ] (optional) I have confirmed this bug exists on the master branch of pandas.

---

```python
# Your code here
import pandas as pd
from matplotlib import pyplot as plt

df = pd.DataFrame({'old_title':[42,73]})
fig,ax = plt.subplots(1,1)
pd.plotting.table(ax,df, colLabels=['new_title'], loc='center')
ax.axis('off')
plt.show()
```

#### Problem description

Setting `rowLabels `or `colLabels `in `pandas.plotting.table` has no effect. I've found that the problem is in `table() `function of **pandas/plotting/_misc.py** as it returns plot_backend.table with predefined rowLabels=None, colLabels=None:
```
    return plot_backend.table(
        ax=ax, data=data, rowLabels=None, colLabels=None, **kwargs
    )
```
It obviously should just pass `rowLabels `and `colLabels ` as is, instead.
Just replace `rowLabels=None, colLabels=None` with `rowLabels=rowLabels, colLabels=colLabels` in line 26 of _misc.py, please.

#### Expected Output

Expected output is a table with column named 'new_title' instead of 'old_title'

Probably something like this (I did not check it would work though, so please try and update as necessary).

```
from unittest.mock import patch
with patch("matplotlib.pyplot.table", return_value=None) as mock_table:

    kwargs = mock_table.call_args.kwargs
    assert kwargs["colLabels"] == ["new_title"]

```
